reasons.speedMPerS: Derived from 'units metal' + 'timestep 0.001' + variable xtip equal "17.8+(step-4000)*dt*10". In metal units dt is the timestep in ps (0.001 ps) and lengths are in Angstrom. Tip advance per step = 10*dt = 10*0.001 = 0.01 A. Tip speed = 0.01 A / 0.001 ps = 10 A/ps. Conversion: 1 A/ps = 1e-10 m / 1e-12 s = 100 m/s, so 10 A/ps = 1000 m/s. (The 10 in the expression is therefore a velocity of 10 A/ps = 1000 m/s, not 10 m/s; '17.8' is only the initial x offset applied from step 4000 onward, and step-4000 zeroes the ramp before that point.)
reasons.fixPrintVariablesValid: Yes for fix print. With 'variable current_step equal step' and 'variable current_time equal time' (both valid equal-style keywords), the double-quoted string '${current_step} ${current_time}' is stored and re-parsed/re-substituted each time the fix fires (every 1 step here), so the printed values track the running step and elapsed time instead of being frozen at definition. This is the key difference from the one-time 'print' command, and it is why the ${...} form is idiomatic inside fix print (the $(...) / v_name forms are the usual belt-and-braces alternative). Caveat: the same string in a plain 'print' command would be substituted once and print a constant. The other keywords shown are also valid: 'screen no' suppresses echoing and 'file variable-print.csv' redirects output, so the snippet is a legal fix print command.
reasons.engineeringStrainValid: Yes. 'variable saved_length equal $(lx)' captures the current box x-length as a number (immediate $() evaluation of the thermo keyword lx), and 'variable L0 equal ${saved_length}' stores that number as a constant, so L0 is frozen at definition time. The strain formula '(lx-v_L0)/v_L0' then mixes a live box length (lx, re-evaluated every time the equal-style variable is used) with the frozen reference length (v_L0, referencing the stored constant), which is exactly the standard engineering-strain definition (L-L0)/L0. Units are consistent in metal units (both in Angstrom, dimensionless ratio). Note the reference comes via v_L0, not L0 directly, which keeps the frozen constant from being re-interpreted.
reasons.eamCanSetMasses: Yes. An EAM setfl file (FeNiCrCoCu-heafixed.setfl) carries a per-element header block containing the atomic mass; pair_style eam/alloy + pair_coeff * * <file> Fe Ni Cr Co Cu maps the five elements to atom types 1-5 and assigns those header masses to the atom types, overwriting the masses that read_data alloy.data had established. This is by design (the potential is parameterized for those masses), so a user-specified Masses section in the data file can legitimately disagree with the setfl header and the setfl values win; LAMMPS does not refuse the load. The practical consequence is that mass-dependent quantities (thermostat coupling, dt limits, velocity rescaling, kinetic temperature) follow the setfl masses, so any deliberate isotopic/custom mass must be re-applied with the 'mass' command after pair_coeff, or the data-file masses made consistent with the potential header.
